correctness.rationale: The two-edge Rademacher wedge expansion is exact. Pairwise orthogonality gives the variance, and all third-degree surviving products are classified into three-stars, triangles, and cross-cut wedges. The sign and normalized-skewness claims follow from an explicit positive derivative factor. Direct exhaustive rational enumeration for all marked scores at n=3..7 agrees; it is a test, not an all-n proof.

value.rationale: The statistic is the canonical nontransitivity count in independently scored complete comparisons. Exact conditional third cumulants settle finite-sample skewness signs for every score and prove a sharp monotonicity of normalized asymmetry under degree balancing. These third-order effects are not visible in pairwise covariances or in classical mean/variance expressions, and are relevant for finite-sample distributional approximations without claiming improved inference.
